# Comment sync (append-only) with persistent Jira-comment-ID map + rich rendering

## Context / Problem
Comment sync identifies comments by **body equality** (normalized-text key in
`outbound_comments._diff_comments`), so same-text comments collide and an edited body
looks new. Semantics are settled as **append-only**: mirror comment *creation* both
ways, never sync edits or deletes.

This story ALSO **owns the DC comment-diff dedup-key migration `3388` deferred here**:
`3388` moves `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` from identity to the rendering form for
descriptions but leaves the comment-diff path on the identity normalizer (a32a
`_resolve_codec` seam, default `_IdentityCodec`), so that cutover does not shift the
comment dedup key. Flipping the comment path to the real codec, and keeping comment-diff
convergent when it renders rich, is this story's job.

## Approach
**1. Identity = local comment key + returned Jira ID, not body.** Local key = the
COMMENT event's **HLC `timestamp`** (unique, monotonic; already on the compiled entry,
`reducer/_processors.py:349`, with `author`). Persist a
**`local_comment_key (HLC) → Jira comment ID`** map in binding state: outbound, an
unmapped key is created in Jira and its returned ID recorded; inbound, mirror Jira
comments whose IDs are not map values (entries carry `jira_comment_id`, bug 85a1,
`_processors.py:354-356`). **Append-only**: no rebar edit/delete pushed to Jira, no Jira
edit/delete applied to rebar; a mapped key/ID is never re-synced. The map is
change-gated, one fixed-shape entry per comment (epic `0303`).

**1a. Capture the returned ID at both enactment sites**, which discard it today. It is
only on `SupportsComments.add_comment`'s returned `{"id": …}` dict
(protocol `_backend.py:540`; Cloud `adapters/jira/backend.py:275`, DC
`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:462` — both delegate to the transport, and the
Cloud transport `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` returns `json.loads(result.stdout)` at
`acli_cli_ops.py:515`, so the `{"id": …}` is present at the return of every deployment's
`add_comment`). So (i) the local key rides ON the mutation
entry as `"local_comment_key": <HLC>`; (ii) `binding_store` reaches both loops:
`create_one` has it; `handle_update` passes `ctx.binding_store`
(`BatchApplyContext.binding_store`) into a new optional `binding_store` param on
`update_one` → `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (BATCH path, `applier._apply_batch`);
`_apply_outbound_update` is threaded from `_apply_typed` for parity. Failures stay
non-fatal (`comment_errors` unchanged). **Crash-durability**: `record_comment_id`
`save()`s immediately on the successful `add_comment` return (write-ahead, per
`binding_store.py:6-28` / `record_pending_key … save()`), closing the DIG-5301 class.

**1b. Two identity stores, one authoritative per DIRECTION, never consulted across
directions.** `jira_comment_id` (bug 85a1) is authoritative for INBOUND-origin comments,
the map for OUTBOUND-origin. **Outbound**: skip when EITHER the HLC key is mapped OR the
comment carries a `jira_comment_id` (inbound-origin, never pushed back); the
normalized-body test (`outbound_comments.py:143`) is DEMOTED, not removed, to a
secondary skip against a lost map write. ID identity is the PRIMARY outbound guard; the
`RECONCILER_MARKER` exclusion (`:72/177-184`) stands.
**Inbound**: `_diff_comments_inbound` (`inbound_differ.py:280`) is UNCHANGED and never
receives the map; its loop-breakers stand — `RECONCILER_MARKER` bodies
(`outbound_comments.py:178`; `inbound_differ.py:337`) and ids matching a local
`jira_comment_id` (`:299,319-321`).

**2. Render bodies through the codec; migrate the dedup key.** Outbound bodies render
through the `RichTextCodec.to_wire` seam descriptions use
(`adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`: `AdfCodec.to_wire` Cloud, the now-rendering
`WikiTextCodec.to_wire` DC after `3388`; Cloud `markdown_to_adf` / `adf_to_markdown` /
`fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` already exist in `adapters/jira/adf.py` from `e59d`). The Cloud
comment path lacks an encode step: descriptions serialize ADF at `acli.py:209`
(`json.dumps(_text_to_adf(_sanitize_description(...)))`), but `acli_cli_ops.add_comment`
(`:492`) sends `--body <str>` (`:510-511`) unencoded — add the ADF encode there.

**ACLI `--body` accepts ADF — VERIFIED, not assumed.** `acli jira workitem comment create
--help` documents `-b, --body string   Comment body in plain text or Atlassian Document
Format (ADF)` (probed on the installed `/opt/homebrew/bin/acli`, exit 0; this is a
read-only `--help`, no Jira mutation). So `--body json.dumps(to_wire(body))` is a supported
surface, exactly as `--description json.dumps(_text_to_adf(...))` already is on the sibling
`workitem edit/create` subcommand. DC's `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` returns a `str`, so DC's
`--body` stays plain wiki text (unchanged).

**Encode/fit/sanitize ORDERING (Cloud, load-bearing).** Today `add_comment` runs the
PLAINTEXT guard `body = _sanitize_comment(body)` (`acli_cli_ops.py:502`, truncating to
`_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS`) BEFORE building `--body`. When the body is ADF-encoded that guard
must NOT run on the serialized JSON: a JSON-serialized ADF document is far longer than its
text and truncating it both mismeasures the true length and can slice the JSON mid-structure,
yielding an ADF payload ACLI rejects. Correct order, mirroring how `AdfCodec.fit_outbound`
already measures the serialized wire: **fit the TEXT first with the rich ADF measure**
(`AdfCodec(rich=...).fit_outbound(body)` → `adf.fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` in rich mode, which
bounds `len(json.dumps(markdown_to_adf(...)))`), **then** `json.dumps(to_wire(fitted))`. The
plaintext `_sanitize_comment` truncation is applied only on the plain-text branch (DC / rich
`off`), never to the serialized ADF. The codec is constructed here the same way
`adapters/jira/backend.py:52,64` do — `AdfCodec(rich="cloud" in cutover_clients())` — so the
`rich_text_cutover` flag (`3388`, ships `off`) governs whether the comment wire renders, with
no capability change when `off` (plain `text_to_adf`, byte-for-byte today's wire).

Then **flip the a32a codec injection** (`_diff_comments`'s `_resolve_codec` argument) from
`_IdentityCodec` to the real `RichTextCodec` so the local dedup key (via
`normalize_outbound`) matches the landed wire.

Depends on `e59d`/`271c`/`3388` shipping first.

## Scope
Engine paths under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:
- `binding_store.py` — map + `record_comment_id(...)` write-ahead writer.
- `outbound_comments.py` — skip logic above; `_map_comments_for_create` (`:148`) and the
  `_diff_comments` append (`:147`) add `"local_comment_key"`; `to_wire` render in
  `_map_comments_for_create`/`_decorate_outbound_comment`; flip `_resolve_codec`.
- `outbound_differ.py` — `compute_outbound_mutations` threads `binding_store` +
  `RichTextCodec` into `_diff_comments` (`:741-743`); `:624` unchanged.
- `dispatch_one.py` — `:418` records the id (`binding_store` at `:154`); `update_one`
  (`:448`) gains the optional param.
- `dispatch_apply_phases.py` `:165` → `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (`:147`).
- `apply_handlers.py` `handle_update` (`:201`) passes `ctx.binding_store` (`:81`);
  `apply_outbound.py` `_apply_outbound_update` (def `:126`, call `:159`) forwards it
  from `_apply_typed` (`applier.py:447`).
- `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py` `add_comment` (`:492`) — Cloud body ADF encode
  (`--body json.dumps(to_wire(fitted))`), fit-then-encode ordering per Approach 2, guarded
  by `AdfCodec(rich="cloud" in cutover_clients())`.
- `reducer/_processors.py` — HLC key (`:349`); `jira_comment_id` (`:354-356`) unchanged.
- `inbound_differ._diff_comments_inbound` (`:280`) — **UNCHANGED, not in the edit set**.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Identity is the persistent COMMENT-HLC → Jira-comment-ID map, not the
  normalized-body key; verified by `test_comment_duplicate_bodies_distinct_ids` (two
  identical-text comments → two IDs).
- [ ] The returned `add_comment` `{"id": …}` is captured at both enactment sites and
  persisted against the originating local key: the entry carries `local_comment_key`;
  `binding_store` reaches both loops (`create_one`; threaded via `update_one` and
  callers `handle_update` / `_apply_outbound_update` into
  `_update_one_dispatch_comments`); `record_comment_id` writes `local_key → id` on Cloud
  (acli) and DC; verified by `test_comment_id_captured_and_persisted`.
- [ ] Inbound-origin `jira_comment_id` (bug 85a1) and the outbound map are each
  authoritative for their own direction and never compete: the inbound differ is
  unchanged, consulting ONLY `RECONCILER_MARKER` / `jira_comment_id`; the outbound
  differ skips when EITHER the key is mapped OR a `jira_comment_id` is present; verified
  by `test_comment_bidirectional_identity_no_double_sync`.
- [ ] Comment sync is append-only both directions — new comments mirror once,
  edits/deletes are not synced; verified by `test_comment_append_only`.
- [ ] Outbound bodies render through `RichTextCodec.to_wire`, with the Cloud comment ADF
  encode on the real create surface (`--body json.dumps(to_wire(fitted))`, where `--body`
  is confirmed by `acli jira workitem comment create --help` to accept ADF) and the
  fit-then-encode ordering (rich `fit_outbound`/`fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` measures the
  serialized wire BEFORE `json.dumps`; the plaintext `_sanitize_comment` guard never
  truncates the serialized JSON) and the `_diff_comments` a32a injection
  migrated from `_IdentityCodec` to the real codec so the dedup key matches the landed
  wire; verified by `test_comment_rendered_through_codec`,
  `test_comment_dedup_key_uses_real_codec`, and
  `test_comment_adf_encode_fits_before_serialize`.
- [ ] After the migration, DC comment-diff converges with zero duplicate re-post
  (counterpart to `3388`'s `test_dc_comment_diff_unchanged_by_cutover`); verified by
  `test_dc_comment_diff_converges_after_migration`.
- [ ] A repeat reconcile pass creates no duplicate comments; verified by
  `test_comment_sync_idempotent`.
- [ ] Crash-durability: `record_comment_id` `save()`s immediately on the successful
  `add_comment` return and the demoted body-equality test stays a secondary skip, so a
  lost map write does not re-post; verified by
  `test_comment_crash_between_add_and_map_save_no_duplicate`.
- [ ] The comment-ID map is change-gated and adds no per-pass churn; verified by the
  git-delta cost harness on a no-new-comment pass.
